findings.title: canManage() grants manage on all groups to admins holding only the VIEW scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, i.e. when the caller has either the `view` or the `manage` scope on the all-groups ("Groups") resource. canManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses via requireManage(), so an admin granted only `view` on all groups can create top-level groups (and anything else gated on groups().canManage()/requireManage()). The per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE; the realm-wide variant should do the same (hasPermission(null, MANAGE)). The interface Javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator even documents this VIEW-or-MANAGE behaviour, so the doc should be fixed too.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and iterates the wrong resources
findings.body: In the V2 schema a per-group authz Resource is created with name == group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup) and without any type set (getOrCreateResource never calls setType). getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() does resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...) which therefore only ever returns the single all-groups type resource, and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). hasPermission() does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so passing the resource UUID never matches and silently falls back to the all-groups resource; and the value added to the set is the authz resource UUID, not a group id. Consequences: (a) the DB-level filtering in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource (session attribute UserModel.GROUPS) and getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds) receive bogus ids — when an admin has view-members/manage-members on all groups, the returned set contains the "Groups" resource UUID and user search/count returns nothing even though canView(user) would allow it; (b) per-group view-members permissions never contribute to the set so the search cannot be narrowed at the DB level and relies solely on post-filtering. The method should use groupResource.getName() both for the permission check and for the collected id, and must iterate the actual per-group resources (e.g. set a type on them in getOrCreateResource, or exclude the type resource). The current tests pass only because the set is empty in the scenarios exercised.

findings.title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body: The Javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false; the implementation checks canManageMembers(GroupModel). Also, the Javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (line 145) says it returns a Stream while the method returns a Set. Misleading API docs for a security-relevant interface.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve display names for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: Groups resources are now created with the raw group id as the resource name (resolveGroup), but getResourceName() only handles the USERS resource type and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). For Groups permissions the admin console/API will show opaque group UUIDs (or null display names) instead of the group name/path, and there is no "All groups" equivalent to the "All users" label. A GROUPS branch mirroring the USERS one should be added.
